tx_main_boulder.blurb: One large limestone boulder with a shallow concave base, set in a shaded spot next to a San Antonio neighborhood near the University of Texas at San Antonio campus. It carries all ten problems, which are mostly V1 and V2 with a single V0 and a single V3, so it suits climbers building up on easy and moderate grades rather than chasing hard projects. Several of the lines pick up top ratings for their quality. It is the first boulder you meet on the short walk down from the trailhead toward the highway bridge, which makes it an easy after-work session for city climbers. Expect a small, low-key spot rather than a destination, and bring a pad.

tx_left_of_the_bow.blurb: A section of the Fiesta Wall limestone boulders beside the Leon Creek Greenway in San Antonio, reached by a short paved walk and a trail along the creek. The ten problems lean easy: eight sit between VB and V1, with one V3 and one V4 for harder tries. The rock is karst limestone with small crimps and a few powerful moves, and traverses stretch the problems into longer outings. Good for beginners or for a quick finger-keeping session. There are no walk-offs, so top-outs mean downclimbing or dropping, and several pads are worth carrying.

tx_wire_wall.blurb: A limestone sport wall in the Weir Dam Area of the Continental Ranch, with a big steel cable crossing the canyon overhead. All ten routes are bolted, starting around 5.10 and climbing through a strong 5.11 band to a handful of 5.12s and two 5.13s, so it is a wall for climbers already comfortable on steeper, harder sport. It is the first wall past the sport line that leads in. The surrounding canyon walls face south and get sun all day, which makes this area a better pick for cool winter days or early starts than for summer afternoons.

tx_whiskey_wall.blurb: A limestone cliff on the east side of the Pecos River gorge in southwest Texas, just above the end of the boat launch. Of its ten routes, nine are sport and one is a 5.7 crack, with most of the sport lines in the 5.10 to 5.11 range and a couple reaching 5.12. The gorge walls are steep, from vertical to slightly overhanging, and call for more technical footwork than the boulder-style climbing common elsewhere in Texas. Bolts here are more than twenty years old and little has been replaced, so inspect hardware before trusting it. Some bases are overgrown with thick brush, so a machete or loppers can help.

tx_sci_fi_wall.blurb: A narrow alleyway between big boulders on the Little Dome side of the Kingdom of Zilch at Enchanted Rock, home to short trad routes, a few boulder problems and some hard face and aid lines. Most of the ten climbs are easy: the trad leads are mainly 5.6 with a couple near 5.10, and the problems run from V0 to V2. You get in by squeezing under a large boulder from the neighboring wall, and the climbs end on a flat ledge above. It is a tight, quirky spot that suits a short session mixed with time on the surrounding building-sized boulders.

tx_wellsite_the.blurb: A water-cut cavern on West Mountain at Hueco Tanks, known as one of the park's most unusual and scenic corners. The cold of the evening lingers inside late into the day, and a small stream sometimes runs through the floor. Of the ten climbs, nine are boulder problems and one is a toprope, with a spread from the lower V2 to V3 range up to a few serious V8 to V10 lines. The walk is straightforward, reached by hiking up slabs and dropping into an opening on the left, and the place sees very few visitors, so it is quiet. Best for strong boulderers who like atmosphere.

tx_wall_of_despair.blurb: A cliff line on the Nolan River near Blum, behind a couple of the area's better-known boulders and reached by following the river downstream. The ten routes are mostly bolted sport with a few trad lines, from one 5.7 up through a cluster of 5.10s to several 5.11 and 5.12 routes. The climbing is short and hard, and the rock is loose, dirty and often covered in moss or lichen. Falling rock is a serious hazard, so avoid standing under anyone climbing. It suits climbers who want a rugged, off-the-beaten-path outing rather than clean, polished stone.
